0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part XV ) was adopred by the Indian Standards Institution on 1 D*:ccmber 1971, sf'tcr thr drart finalized by the Rubber Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 In some rubber vulcanizates it may be essential to fulfil the safety requirements along with antistatic properties. In such cases normally lower limit of resistance of 5 X lo4 ohms for 2X volt mains should be specified. As the resistance depends on lhe strain, temperature and rate of generation of charge, the safety requirements may not be recommended unless standard conditions are specified. 0.3 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

4.TBSTPIECE
4.1 The test specimen shall be in the form of flat plate with width between 10 to 15 mm, length between 70 to 150 mm and thickness approximately The thickness 2 mm uniform all over with a tolerance of f 1 percent. between different test pieces shall not vary by more than 5 percent. Standard dumb-bell mould test pieces may be used provided the surface of the uncured rubber is kept free of soap stone or any other mould lubricant. To avoid surface distortion while `removing from the mould, the test pieces shall be moulded between moisture sensitive cellophane paper .whlch can be readily removed after briefimmersion in Mater. The paper should be removed without bending or scratching and should be patted dry. If specimen is to be collected from a product, the test piece is to be It can be cleaned cut from the portion where it is not buffed or abraided. with Fuller's earth and water and washed with distilled water and dried in air. The specimen should be uniform in thickness and should not be distorted during preparation. 5. GGNDlTIGNING 5.1 The time between &lcanization and testing shall not be less than For finished 16 hours and not more than 6 days for moulded specimen. products, this shall lx not more than 2 months after receipt by the customer. 5.2 The specimen shall be conditioned for at least 16bhours and tested at a temperature of 27 ;t 2�C and a relative humidity of 65 percent, 5

18:34OO(PartXV)-1971 5.3 Immediately prior to the test, the current electrodes shall be connected to the end of test piece by grips extending to 5 cm along the test piece and heated on a sheet of hinhly insulating material for 2 hours at 70 f 2�C to remove strains or irregularities and aliowed to cool for at least one hour and tested at room temperature without any disturbance to the test piece. 6. PROCEDURE 6.1 For Plate Type Electrode-Measure the dimensions of the electrodes and determine the effective area of the measuring electrode and width of the guard gap. Measure the volume resistance between electrodes No. 1 and 3 (see Fig. 1 ) with a suitable device hiving the Unless otherwise specified, the time required sensitivity and accuracy, of electrification shall be 1 min and the applied direct voltage swl be 500 f 5 v. 6.2 For Contact Point Electrode 6.2.1 The test piece, milliammeter and electrometer having an inpur resistance greater than 101s ohms shall be arranged as shown in Fig.' 3.
